criteria.build_driving_ops: Treat the absent execution paths as a platform gap and close it: ship Can catalogue operations plus runtime and qualification for supervising a genuine Chromium over CDP (navigate, click, evaluate, cookie-store reads, CSP-violation events) alongside a test HTTPS client that accepts self-signed fixtures, then carry C02/C03 over with zero blocked legs and remove the runners. Nothing in the browser queues ships until the platform work lands and qualifies.
criteria.defer_browser_queues: Take no browser-queue action now: the 2 delivery runners, the 3 preview sources and document, and the 5 deliverable fixtures stay byte-identical while the other 6 open records close, and C02/C03/C04 reopen only on new findings or new primitives. The run avoids partial ports, blocked-leg records, and platform construction in this area; remaining effort goes to the portable queues.
criteria.port_wire_with_blocked: Harvest the portable majority immediately with the in-process recipe (staged production routes behind server_start/stop, fetch_bytes driver, descriptor-judged SQL, sqlite3-owned DDL): issuance/claim/redirect chains, wire cookie strings, security-header text, statuses, grant and state rows, file bytes, and restart behavior, including all of S04 and plain-HTTP versions of transport-incidental TLS legs, with the one-shot race covered back-to-back. Switch C02/C03 onto the C01 producer, erase the 5 C04 originals, and log Chromium-enforced plus TLS-listener checks as blocked legs citing the exact missing primitive. The legacy runners survive solely for those blocked legs; the runtime stays untouched.

browser_scope.instructions: Select the browser-queue strategy that disposes all 28 migration records truthfully while keeping every retained check either live in Can or explicitly accounted for.

state.baselines: Four harnesses define the browser scope. tests/site_delivery/proof.mjs (171 lines, 9 PASS groups) steers Chromium through Playwright at an openssl self-signed origin. tests/site_delivery/strict-redirect.mjs (90 lines) covers redirect-and-cookie chains. tests/site_preview/probe.ts (279 lines, S03) blends Can issuance, SQLite, HTTPS, and browser legs. tests/site_preview/approval_probe.ts (168 lines, S04) is plain HTTP plus SQLite plus staged files, with no browser and no TLS. C01's fixture producer stands complete; C04 erases 5 fixture files when C02/C03 read from it.
state.browser_only_legs: A fixed set of checks cannot execute under any present Can operation: live page-script execution with DOM, style, font, and media readback (fixtureReady, getComputedStyle, fonts.ready, naturalWidth, clicks), an authentic cookie store (__Host- rules, HttpOnly, SameSite, carriage across redirects, forgery refusal), in-browser CSP violation signals (securitypolicyviolation), navigation with default versus overridden referrers, and worker/serviceworker gating. About 5 of the 9 proof.mjs groups require them; so do strict-redirect.mjs's form-action denial and click-chain cookie assertions and the final probe.ts lines 227-277 pair of groups.
state.mandate: The language is authored by AI agents and carries no duty to prior spellings, binaries, or goldens; project law puts goal attainment ahead of scaffolding volume and proof layering. Twenty-eight baseline records under manolea-2/tests migrate one by one, each host file disappearing only after its surviving legs pass as live Can verdicts on true production behavior, with F01 reconciling the set. Work happens on a 256 GB MacBook, so spare disk and machine load are firm ceilings.
state.mechanism_inventory: In-process DOM emulation is the whole of the 44 browser:: catalogue operations (mount/query/event/state verbs); navigation, cookie storage, network calls, TLS handling, CDP, and external browser command appear in none of them (catalogue grep verified). Plain-HTTP wire verification rides on http::fetch_bytes, qualified live 13/13 on 2026-10-02, with repeated ?query keys and manual redirect handling. Twelve records stand fulfilled on precisely those mechanisms, and no completed port has called for browser driving.
state.portable_legs: Wire-visible assertions dominate and match the proven in-process recipe: staged production site_routes served via server_start/stop, an http::fetch_bytes driver, probe-owned SQL descriptors for seed and verdict, DDL via /usr/bin/sqlite3. Covered: grant/claim/303 sequences, set-cookie wire strings, CSP, referrer-policy, and cache-control header text, status codes, SQLite grant, expiry, revocation, and state rows, exact file bytes, restart persistence. S04 moves over entirely, contingent on one mounting answer (exchange() currently calls the TypeScript createPreviewHandler in-process, so the Can version needs a sibling Can production preview route, not yet confirmed to exist). The S03 Promise.all race converts to sequential claims establishing second-claim refusal, keeping simultaneity as a named blocked leg.
state.tls_position: Only the server half of TLS is present (http::server_start_tls). Fixture handshakes fail client-side: Bun fetch dies on 'self signed certificate' (demonstrated 2026-10-02), with no insecure switch or test-CA path in http::fetch_bytes. openssl stays usable for creating fixture certificates under process::run. Because S03's TLS legs assert transport-independent facts, they keep their meaning over plain HTTP; the single transport-native check, serving correctly from a TLS listener, collapses to a bind-success leg.
